title: विनिर्माणवादी दर्शन र भाषा शिक्षणको सम्बन्ध {The relation of constructivist philosophy and language teaching}
authors: थापा Thapa, ढाल बहादुर Dhal Bahadur
nepali: प्रस्तुत लेखमा ज्याक डेरिडाको विनिर्माणवाद र भाषा शिक्षणमा विनिर्माणवादको सम्बन्धका बारेमा अध्ययन गरिएको छ । डेरिडाको विनिर्माणवादलाई उत्तर संरचनावादको विशिष्ट सिद्धान्त मानिन्छ । यो दार्शनिक क्षेत्रबाट साहित्यिक क्षेत्रमा प्रवेश गरेको अवधारणा हो । यो लेख तयार पार्नका निम्ति पुस्तकालय स्रोतको प्रयोग गरिएको छ । यसको अध्ययन विधि विश्लेषणात्मक तथा व्याख्यात्मक रहेको छ । कुनै विषय क्षेत्रलाई फेरि अर्को शिराबाट हेर्नु, सोच्नु तथा अध्ययन गर्नु नै विनिर्माणवाद हो । डेरिडाको विनिर्माणवाद र फरकपना भाषा तथा साहित्यका क्षेत्रमा बहूपयोगी सिद्ध हुनसक्ने देखिएको छ । नेपालको नीति निर्माण, कार्यान्वयन तथा भाषा शिक्षणमा विनिर्माणवादको आवश्यकता खड्कदो रहेको छ । ज्याक डेरिडाको विनिर्माणवाद त्यसको फरकपना र भाषा शिक्षणमा सम्बन्धका बारेमा जानकारी राख्न चाहनेलागि यो लेख महत्वपूर्ण सावित हुनेछ छ ।
american_english: In the present article, a study has been made of Jacques Derrida's deconstruction and of the relationship of deconstruction to language teaching. Derrida's deconstruction is regarded as a distinctive theory of post-structuralism. It is a concept that moved into the literary field from the philosophical field. Library sources were used in order to prepare this article. Its method of study is analytical and interpretive. To look at a subject area again from another angle, to think about it and to study it — that itself is deconstruction. Derrida's deconstruction and its difference appear likely to prove highly useful in the fields of language and literature. The need for deconstruction is looming large in Nepal's policy making, policy implementation and language teaching. This article will prove important for anyone who wants to have some knowledge about Jacques Derrida's deconstruction, its difference, and its relationship to language teaching.
british_english: The present piece sets out to examine Jacques Derrida's deconstruction and the bearing that deconstruction has upon the teaching of language. Derrida's deconstruction is held to be a distinctive theory of post-structuralism. It is a notion that made its way into the literary field out of the philosophical field. Library sources have been drawn upon in the preparation of this article. Its method of study is analytical and interpretative. To view a subject area afresh from another vantage point, to ponder it and to study it, is deconstruction itself. Derrida's deconstruction and its difference look set to prove of considerable service in the fields of language and literature. The need for deconstruction is pressing ever harder upon policy making, policy implementation and language teaching in Nepal. This article will prove of value to anyone wishing to be informed about Jacques Derrida's deconstruction, its difference and its relation to language teaching.
australian_english: This article looks at Jacques Derrida's deconstruction and at how deconstruction relates to language teaching. Derrida's deconstruction is reckoned to be a particular theory of post-structuralism. It's an idea that came across into the literary field from the philosophical one. Library sources were used to put this article together. The way it's studied is analytical and interpretive. Looking at a subject area again from another angle, thinking it through and studying it — that's deconstruction. Derrida's deconstruction and its difference look like being really handy in the fields of language and literature. The need for deconstruction is really making itself felt in Nepal's policy making, policy implementation and language teaching. This article will be a worthwhile read for anyone wanting a bit of knowledge about Jacques Derrida's deconstruction, its difference and its link with language teaching.
informal_english: This piece digs into Jacques Derrida's deconstruction and how it ties in with teaching language. People treat Derrida's deconstruction as one of the standout theories of post-structuralism. It's an idea that crossed over from philosophy into literature. I leaned on library sources to put the article together. The way it's studied is analytical, and it's interpretive too. Taking a subject area and looking at it again from a different angle, thinking on it, studying it — that's deconstruction right there. Derrida's deconstruction and his idea of difference look like they could be a whole lot of use in language and literature. Nepal needs deconstruction more and more when it comes to making policy, carrying it out, and teaching language. So if you want to know a thing or two about Jacques Derrida's deconstruction, about difference, and about how it all connects to language teaching, this article will do you some good.
translator_notes: The Nepali term विनिर्माणवाद is rendered as 'deconstruction' in line with its attribution to Derrida; फरकपना is rendered as 'difference'. Sentence order follows the source exactly.
